messages:
Alex: Quick sync — we need a practical plan for customer migration windows for Private (VPC/on‑prem) installs, esp customers that require fully offline/airgapped upgrades. I want clear launch gating and a list of exceptions we can support.
Maria: +1. Constraints we keep hitting: customer network change freezes, DB schema migrations that need quiesce, and legal blackout windows for high-reg clients. Typical ask is 'no more than 4h outage' but many expect 0-downtime.
Dmitri: For airgapped installs we can't rely on live package repo. We should support two modes: "staged airgap" (images + manifest shipped to customer) and "operator-push" (customer runs operator to pull from internal registry).
Sarah: Preflight and drift detection are crucial. Propose an automated preflight that checks: static IPs, DNS entries, cert validity, BGP routes (if used), and reachable KMS endpoints. Fail fast with clear remediation hints.
ops-bot: Deploy checklist: https://intranet.redwood/tools/offline-deploy-checklist (pinned). Also CI job: `airgap-manifest-verify` runs signatures + SLSA provenance for shipped bundles. :lock:
Luis: Note on KMS/HSM: offline customers often use hardware HSMs with key rotation policies. If we change encryption envelope during upgrade we need a rekey path that doesn't force full restore. Ops dependency.
Emily: Rollback story — must be able to toggle to previous operator/controller image and ideally keep schema-compatible migrations. If a DB migration is risky, we should support feature-flagging new behavior behind rollout flags.
Maria: Scheduling rules suggestion: default window = 02:00 customer local time, 2hr target, 4hr hard cap. Allow exceptions: long-running DB migrations (preapproved), regulatory freeze weeks (end of quarter), and emergency security patch windows.
Alex: Launch gating checklist draft (for product + eng + SE signoff):
- Preflight pass rate >= 95% on staged customers
- Offline manifest verification + provenance signatures
- Rollback validated in 3 different customer topologies (NAT-only, BGP, strict firewall)
- Runbook & runbook-drill completed with SEs for first 5 customers
- Automated post-upgrade smoke checks (inbound API, KV cache warm, latencies)
Dmitri: Technical note — we should implement `--maintenance-window` in the upgrade controller so operator can provide start + duration and controller enforces drain/restore steps. Pseudocode:```bash
redwoodctl upgrade --customer-id=acme --maintenance-window="2025-01-10T02:00Z/02:00" --mode=airgap
```
Sarah: Also add a `--no-db-migrate` flag for cases where we do an operator upgrade but postpone schema migration until a separate maintenance. Must be explicit in runbook.
Luis: For customer-managed networking: require a network contract template listing static egress IPs, port openings, and optional BGP ASN advertisement. This reduces last-minute firewall surprises.
Emily: Ops training: every SE doing an airgap rollout should run one dry-run in staging with a simulated cold-registry. Have a certification checklist.
Alex: Good. Action items: Maria to draft exceptions policy and maintenance window defaults; Dmitri to spec controller flags + CLI; Sarah to outline preflight checks and smoke tests; Luis to draft network contract template; Emily to draft SE training checklist. We'll sync next Tue. :calendar:
